name:
Tian et al. 2018
AVEL
title: Audio-Visual Event Localization in Unconstrained Videos
question: Can a model identify the class and time of an event that is both visible and audible? Introduces AVE tasks, the dataset and audio-guided visual attention.
modalities: Audio and RGB video. Segment labels in fully supervised learning and clip labels in weak supervision. Precomputed VGG-19 and AudioSet audio features. Both modalities are available at inference.
mechanism: A+V-att weights visual regions using audio and concatenates two BiLSTM outputs. The paper describes cross-entropy. The inspected training script uses MultiLabelSoftMarginLoss.
data: AVE contains 4,143 clips and 28 event classes. Original split sizes are 3,339/402/402. Ten one-second segments per clip, with an additional background class.
evidence: Table 1 reports fully/weakly supervised A+V-att at 72.7%/66.7%. Audio-only 59.5%, video-only 55.3%, A+V without attention 71.4%. DMRN is a separate fusion model.
resources: Code, weights and precomputed features are available. Original Python 3.6/PyTorch 0.3.0. This project adapts the published checkpoint at a pinned revision for CPU inference.
limits: A+V-att is the reproduction target. Retaining original labels during controlled shifts tests event recovery under clock errors. This project does not reproduce training.

name:
Xuan et al. 2020
CMAN
title: Cross-Modal Attention Network for Temporal Inconsistent Audio-Visual Event Localization
question: How should a model select spatial, temporal and modal evidence under inconsistency? Combines spatial attention, self-attention and adaptive co-attention.
modalities: Audio and RGB, fully and weakly supervised. Evidence for an event may occur at different seconds across modalities. The paper identifies its visual backbone as ResNet-151.
mechanism: An LSTM sentinel gate weighs within-modality memory against context from the other modality. Three attention mechanisms support the shared localization objective.
data: AVE with an 80%/10%/10% split. Sixteen RGB frames per second. VGG-like audio features and the ResNet visual features reported in the paper.
evidence: Table 1 reports 77.1%/75.7%. Disabling the attention modules gives 71.4%/69.0%. Removing the sentinel gives 76.1%/74.9% in Table 2.
resources: Architecture and preprocessing are described. Official code, a released checkpoint and hardware details were not verified in the initial search.
limits: Studies natural inconsistency. Main tables do not separate fixed offset magnitudes. The gate ablation illustrates how to examine modality selection.

name:
Zhou et al. 2021
PSP
title: Positive Sample Propagation Along the Audio-Visual Event Line
question: Can useful audio-visual pairs at different seconds share evidence? Propagates features through strong positive connections.
modalities: Audio and RGB, fully and weakly supervised. Related pairs need not share a time index. Uses VGG-19 and VGG-like audio features.
mechanism: Computes all-pair audio-visual similarities after BiLSTMs, removes weak links and propagates features. Fully supervised training adds a pair-similarity loss to classification.
data: AVE segment accuracy. Repository includes HDF5 split lists and labels. A common dataset alone does not establish identical evaluation protocols across papers.
evidence: Table 1 reports 77.8%/73.5%. Removing PSP gives 73.7%/70.2%. Keeping all connections gives 75.9% in fully supervised learning.
resources: PyTorch code, features and checkpoints are linked. The fully supervised README threshold is 0.099, whereas Table 3 reports the best threshold as 0.095.
limits: Cross-time positive-pair selection directly motivates the project. The threshold and pair loss would need separate evaluation under controlled shifts.

name:
Xia and Zhao 2022
CMBS
title: Cross-Modal Background Suppression for Audio-Visual Event Localization
question: Does suppressing irrelevant temporal and event evidence from the other modality improve localization? Introduces temporal and event-level background suppression.
modalities: Audio and RGB, fully and weakly supervised. An event in only one modality may be background for joint localization. VGG-19 and Res-151 visual variants are reported separately.
mechanism: Generates temporal gates and event scores from the other modality. Event classification and gate supervision suppress irrelevant cross-modal evidence.
data: AVE segment accuracy with fixed audio features. VGG-19 and Res-151 visual-backbone comparisons are reported separately.
evidence: VGG-19 results are 79.3%/74.2%. Removing temporal suppression gives 77.93%/73.45%. Removing event suppression gives 78.30%/73.57%.
resources: Code, configurations, features and checkpoints are linked. Repository specifies Python 3.7.6, PyTorch 1.10.2 and CUDA 11.4.
limits: Background suppression and compensating for a clock offset are distinct mechanisms. Delayed but relevant audio could be mistakenly suppressed.

name:
Liu et al. 2025
AVSGN
title: Audio-Visual Semantic Graph Network for Audio-Visual Event Localization
question: Can class texts provide shared semantics and cross-time interaction? Uses subgraphs over three modalities to propagate semantic relationships.
modalities: Audio, RGB and known class texts rather than clip-specific transcripts. Uses CLIP Swin-V2-L and CLAP HTS-AT features.
mechanism: CMSA maps modalities to a shared space. CMGI builds audio-visual, audio-text and visual-text subgraphs. Objectives include classification, event relevance, gating and semantic consistency.
data: AVE fully/weakly supervised segment accuracy. CLIP/CLAP provide 512-dimensional features, unlike the VGG-based features used by Tian et al.
evidence: Table 1 reports 83.1%/78.8%. Removing the audio-visual subgraph gives 80.3%/75.9%. Removing all three subgraphs gives 79.6%/74.8%.
resources: Reports PyTorch, RTX 2080 Ti, 200 epochs and Adam. Official code and a method-specific checkpoint were not verified in the initial search.
limits: Cross-paper score differences also reflect backbone changes. Within-system subgraph ablations provide a closer test of the graph contribution.
